hardware.name: Concealed cup hinges

hardware.name: Face vise screw
notes: Bore 1-1/8" through both jaws for the screw, as its maker says.
Opens to 8".
One guide bar: bore 7/8" for each, 5" from the screw's center.
Mount the nut with 4 wood screws, of the size its maker says.

hardware.name: End vise screw
notes: Bore 1-1/8" through both jaws for the screw, as its maker says.

Two guide bars: bore 7/8" for each, 4" from the screw's center.

hardware.name: Lower drawer slides, 14"

hardware.name: Wood screws, 1" long
notes: Through each box front into its drawer front, two to a drawer. Length: the box front’s 1/2" plus about two-thirds of the drawer front’s 13/16", to the nearest quarter inch, so the points stop 5/16" short of its show face.
Gauge: ask the hardware supplier which size suits hardwood of that thickness, and what pilot hole it needs.

hardware.name: Wood screws, 1-1/2" long, with washers
notes: Up through the slot at the back of each drawer bottom into the box back’s lower edge, one to a drawer, with a washer so the bottom can slide under the head. Length: the bottom’s 1/2" plus about twice the box back’s 1/2" thickness into its edge, to the nearest quarter inch.
Leave it snug, not tight, and never glue the bottom: it moves front to back with the seasons.

hardware.name: Wood glue

flags.ask: Ask an experienced builder whether the back legs' mortises, 3/16" longer toward the back, leave the top room to move against tenons glued at the front.
flags.why: The top moves across its 17-5/8" depth with the seasons, and the legs' tenons go through it 13-5/8" apart. The Wood Movement section estimates how much.

flags.ask: Ask an experienced builder whether the 5" of top past the legs at each end carries heavy work there, such as chopping or work held in the end vise.
flags.why: Kerf computes only the top’s sag between the legs, not what it carries past them.

flags.ask: Ask an experienced builder whether screws for the upper drawers’ slides, driven into both faces of the divider at the same height, will meet inside it.
flags.why: Screws longer than half the divider’s 3/4" meet in the middle when the holes line up. Staggering the two slides’ holes, or shorter screws, avoids it.

checklist.element: The base: legs, feet, and rails
checklist.confirm: Confirm with an experienced builder that the glued mortises and tenons keep the base square and steady when planing pushes the top along and across.
checklist.why: Hand planing pushes hard on a bench, and Kerf does not compute joint strength.

checklist.element: The bench with a vise open
checklist.confirm: Confirm whether the bench can tip when planing at an end past the legs, or with work in an open vise.
checklist.why: The top runs past the legs at each end, and a vise holds work farther out still.

checklist.element: The through tenons and the back mortises
checklist.confirm: Confirm with an experienced builder how much glue the front tenons through the top need, and that the back tenons stay unglued in their long mortises.
checklist.why: The top holds the frame together at its tenons, and gluing the back ones would stop it moving.

checklist.element: Glue lines in the top and legs
checklist.confirm: Confirm with an experienced builder that the strips of the top and legs are glued well enough for heavy work.
checklist.why: Kerf does not compute the strength of glue lines.

checklist.element: Bending and shear of the top
checklist.confirm: Confirm the top is strong enough, not only stiff enough.
checklist.why: There are no published design values for furniture lumber, so Kerf checks only deflection.

checklist.confirm: Confirm with an experienced builder that the dovetailed boxes suit what goes in them.
checklist.why: Tools are heavy, and Kerf computes nothing for the drawers.

movement.subject: Top, between its front and back tenons

flags.ask: Ask an experienced builder whether the back legs' mortises, 1/4" longer toward the back, leave the top room to move against tenons glued at the front.
flags.why: The top moves across its 17-5/8" depth with the seasons, and the legs' tenons go through it 13-5/8" apart. The Wood Movement section estimates how much.

flags.ask: Ask an experienced builder whether the 5" of top past the legs at each end carries heavy work there, such as chopping or work held in the end vise.
flags.why: Kerf computes only the top’s sag between the legs, not what it carries past them.

flags.ask: Ask an experienced builder whether screws for the upper drawers’ slides, driven into both faces of the divider at the same height, will meet inside it.
flags.why: Screws longer than half the divider’s 3/4" meet in the middle when the holes line up. Staggering the two slides’ holes, or shorter screws, avoids it.

checklist.element: The base: legs, feet, and rails
checklist.confirm: Confirm with an experienced builder that the glued mortises and tenons keep the base square and steady when planing pushes the top along and across.
checklist.why: Hand planing pushes hard on a bench, and Kerf does not compute joint strength.

checklist.element: The bench with a vise open
checklist.confirm: Confirm whether the bench can tip when planing at an end past the legs, or with work in an open vise.
checklist.why: The top runs past the legs at each end, and a vise holds work farther out still.

checklist.element: The through tenons and the back mortises
checklist.confirm: Confirm with an experienced builder how much glue the front tenons through the top need, and that the back tenons stay unglued in their long mortises.
checklist.why: The top holds the frame together at its tenons, and gluing the back ones would stop it moving.

checklist.element: Glue lines in the top and legs
checklist.confirm: Confirm with an experienced builder that the strips of the top and legs are glued well enough for heavy work.
checklist.why: Kerf does not compute the strength of glue lines.

checklist.element: Bending and shear of the top
checklist.confirm: Confirm the top is strong enough, not only stiff enough.
checklist.why: There are no published design values for furniture lumber, so Kerf checks only deflection.

checklist.confirm: Confirm with an experienced builder that the dovetailed boxes suit what goes in them.
checklist.why: Tools are heavy, and Kerf computes nothing for the drawers.

assumptions: All of it sits at the middle of the span, where the top bends most.
The top runs past the legs and is held by their tenons; taking it as simply supported overstates its deflection.
The dog holes and the mortises take a little out of the section and are left out, which understates it slightly.
Simply supported between the two supports.
E is the average for small, clear, straight-grained specimens; boards with knots or cross grain may be less stiff.
E includes shear deflection, so bending deflection alone is computed.
E is at 12% moisture content; most properties increase as wood dries below that, so drier indoor wood is stiffer.
No NDS adjustment factors apply to a clear-wood value.
formulas: For each load P at a (b = L − a): δ(x) = P·b·x·(L² − b² − x²) / (6·E·I·L) for x ≤ a, mirrored for x ≥ a

Δ_T(x) = K_cr · Δ_LT(x) + Δ_ST(x); δ = largest Δ_T over the span
